Young Drive, South Los Angeles, CA 90095-1766, msuchard@ucla.edu; @suchard_group, Rohan Khera MD, MS, 195 Church Street, 6th Floor, New Haven, CT 06510, rohan.khera@yale.edu; @rohan_khera

Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP1-RAs) reduce major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, their effectiveness relative to each other and other second-line antihyperglycemic agents is unknown, without any major ongoing head-to-head trials.

To compare the cardiovascular effectiveness of SGLT2is, GLP1-RAs, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4is), and sulfonylureas (SUs) as second-line antihyperglycemic agents in T2DM.
